html:
SMTO-CFG-0069 — The Gateway doesn't know your SMTO server's address

GUID: d1389af5-4f79-49aa-bfb2-95c927daf43a
Slug: outbound-host-required
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: cfg

What happened

  • The Gateway, the helper program SMTO uses to run commands on a computer, was started to connect out to SMTO, but it wasn't given the SMTO server's address, so it stopped.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Find your SMTO server's address and port. They're usually in the web address you use to open SMTO, for example 192.168.1.10 and 8011. The Gateway needs this exact address to reach the server.
  2. On the Gateway computer, start it with that address, for example: ./src/gateway_agent/startup.sh --server-host 192.168.1.10 --server-port 8011 --server-scheme https (use http if your SMTO web address starts with http://). Giving a server address tells the Gateway where to connect; without it the Gateway has nowhere to go.
  3. On Windows, use .\src\gateway_windows\startup.ps1 with -ServerHost, -ServerPort and -ServerScheme https. On a Mac, use ./src/gateway_macos/startup.sh with the same options as Linux. Each computer type has its own start script, but they all need the same three values.
  4. In SMTO, open Settings › Setup › Gateways. Once the Gateway connects it appears in the list; make sure Enabled is turned on for it. A Gateway that is listed but not enabled isn't used for new Tasks.

What success looks like

  • The Gateway window no longer shows this message, and the Gateway becomes available for new Tasks in SMTO.

If it still fails

  • Copy the full message from the Gateway window, or select Copy error details if it appears in SMTO, and send it with the address you used to the person who manages SMTO. Don't change Gateway timeouts or other settings; only the server address is missing.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The outbound Gateway client stopped at startup because GATEWAY_SERVER_HOST (settings.server_host) was empty after configuration was resolved.

What this means

  • Starting the outbound Gateway client finds no configured server_host. The owning policy, configuration or publication transaction validates this state. Diagnostics do not grant authority, replace accepted snapshots, execute capabilities or publish a site; preserve the exact current decision and evidence.

Why this can happen

  • Starting the outbound Gateway client finds no configured server_host.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect GATEWAY_SERVER_HOST and its paired port/scheme on the Gateway host.

How to fix it

  • Set GATEWAY_SERVER_HOST (or --server-host / -ServerHost) together with GATEWAY_SERVER_PORT and GATEWAY_SERVER_SCHEME (http or https, matching how the Server is served) in the Gateway host's environment or startup command, and make sure saved managed Gateway settings don't clear it. Restart that Gateway once its active work has settled; on its first outbound handshake the Server registers it under Settings › Setup › Gateways.
  • Set GATEWAY_SERVER_HOST in the Gateway host configuration to the intended controller host, then restart that Gateway when active work is settled.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended controller address is configured and outbound startup reaches normal authenticated connection checks.

What not to do

  • Do not change an unrelated timeout, budget or policy. Check whether the named setting applies only to a new task.

Technical notes

  • The owning policy, configuration or publication transaction validates this state. Diagnostics do not grant authority, replace accepted snapshots, execute capabilities or publish a site; preserve the exact current decision and evidence.
